 title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: /img//wolverine.png background-opacity: "0.45" format: revealjs: chalkboard: true multiplex: true scrollable: true --- ## Goal ```{=html} ``` To consider modeling decisions and tradeoffs: -

## Case Study ![](/img//wolverine.image.png) ## ![](/img//wafwa.png){fig-align="center" width=40%} ## Sampling Frame ![](/img//wafwa_sampling.png){fig-align="center" width=40%} ## Station Setup ![](/img//wafwa_station.png){fig-align="center"} ## Project Goals - **Primary:** To map winter wolverine distributions across the western U.S. to track changes in occurence over time (i.e., contraction or expansion) . . . - **Secondary:** To understand the factors that govern wolverine occurence in the western United States. ## Modeling Option 1 **Naive Occupancy:** $\hat{\psi} = \frac{\sum y_i}{n}$, $y \in \{0,1\}$ ## Modeling Option 2 **Fit occupancy model with covariates:** $$ \begin{align*} \textbf{y}_{i} \sim& \text{Binomial}(z_i\times p_{i}, J)\\ z_i \sim& \text{Bernoulli}(\psi_i)\\ \text{logit}(\psi_{i}) =& \alpha_0 + \alpha_1 \times \text{human.mod}_{i} + \\ &\alpha_2 \times \text{elev}_{i} + \alpha_3 \times \text{snow.depth}_{i} \\ \text{logit}(p_{i}) =& \beta_0 \\ \end{align*} $$ ## Modeling Option 2a {.scrollable} **Predict occupancy for the whole sampling frame** . I.e., prediction with covariates. . . . ![](/img//wolverine_covs.png){fig-align="center" width=120% .nostretch} ## Modeling Option 2b **Predict occupancy only at sampled sites** ![](/img//wafwa_2017_dets.png){fig-align="center" width=70% .nostretch} ## Modeling Option 3 **Multi-model comparison; predict occupancy at the whole sampling frame or only sampled sites** ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |model |AIC |DeltaAIC |AIC.Weights | |:-----------------------------------|:---|:--------|:-----------| |psi ~ 1 | | | | |psi ~ human.mod | | | | |psi ~ elev | | | | |psi ~ snow.depth | | | | |psi ~ human.mod + elev + snow.depth | | | | ::: ::: ## Modeling Option 4a {.scrollable} **Predictions from a spatial occupancy model at the whole sampling frame**. For example, intrinsic conditional autoregressive model (ICAR). - covariates are not needed - leverages 'closeness' of the detection data to estimate occupancy . . . ![](/img//spatial_occ_map.png){fig-align="center" width=80% .nostretch} ## Modeling Option 4b {.scrollable} **Predictions from a spatial occupancy model WITH COVARIATES at the whole sampling frame**. - can add covariates on detection or occupancy - the spatial process and spatial covariates are not necessarily uniquely identifiable (inference may be unclear) ## Modeling Option 5 **Prediction from a non-linear supervised machine learning algorithm at the whole sampling frame**. For example, 'random forests', 'gradient boosting', 'maximum entropy'. - covariates required - non-linear relationships are handled - correlation among variables is fine - trains model based on cross validation ## To do - Group up and discuss - List out the benefits/costs of each option, in terms of objectives 1 and 2. - What option would you pick? Why? - If you make your own chimera option (mix match model type and model fitting), you need to say why it's better and how practical it is to accomplish. - Can ask me questions ## Options Summary 1) Naive occupancy 2) Single occupancy model, predict --> sampling frame OR sampled sites 3) Multi-model occupancy approach, predict --> sampling frame OR sampled sites 4) Single spatial occupancy model. No covariates or with covariates. Predict --> sampling frame 5) Non-linear supervised machine learning algorithm. Predict --> sampling frame

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
